sources.assumptions: Explicit modeling assumptions recorded per food and below; not verified brand values.

unicoPasteLabel.description: Per 30 mL: calcium 10 mg, iron 0.4 mg, potassium 300 mg.

notes: Micronutrient planning estimates for the current plan, not a measurement or product-label audit. Units match nutrition_basis.json; breakfast inputs are per 100 g. Numeric coverage is explicit; a missing field causes recalculation to fail.

Generic CNF 2026 edible raw weights match the plan. Cooking/draining losses are not modeled; branded convenience foods use generic proxies when no label data are available. These estimates must not be used to diagnose a nutrient deficiency. No invented confidence intervals.

Iodine varies substantially. Egg iodine uses the boiled-egg proxy of 31 mcg each for all 18 eggs/week. Chicken cooked yield assumed75% for the roasted thigh proxy0.7 mcg/85 g. Salmon uses NIH/USDA cooked salmon11 mcg/85 g at75% yield. Haddock250 mcg/110 g raw is based on only3 USDA samples (range152–345 per110 g); 100 g fish per breaded fillet is assumed. Tuna7.4 mcg/85 g drained. Beef proxy6.4 mcg/85 g scaled to85 g meatball unit. Commercial salts are not automatically iodized; low-iodine plant/condiment allowances are estimates, not verified zeros.

Unquantified dry seasoning beyond noodle sauce, drinking-water minerals and zero-calorie beverages are omitted from these six micronutrient totals. Creatine contributes none. Fruit tray composition and kiwi edible size are assumptions.
Macro/calorie data remain unchanged by this micronutrient completion. Breakfast and drink mineral estimates are recalculated from the same documented ingredients instead of retaining old totals.

oil.basis: One teaspoon olive oil; trace minerals ignored, vitamins D/B12 absent.

salt.basis: One teaspoon assumed 6 g. Canadian table salt 0.01% potassium iodide; iodine fraction 126.9/166.0 gives 458.7 mcg. Only separately added salt counted; no iodization assumed for processed-food sodium. No cooking/storage-loss correction.

curry.basis: S&B label per 18 g: Ca, Fe, K and D. B12 absent from plant-based unfortified ingredients; iodine unmeasured, trace contribution omitted.

dumpling.basis: Per four dumplings/96 g excluding sauce: surrogate 30 g dry wheat flour, 25 g cabbage, 25 g raw ground chicken and 16 g water. Ratios assumed, not manufacturer recipe; iodine trace estimate 0.2 mcg.

noodleSauce.basis: One meal: fish sauce 3 g, combined soy sauces 5.3 g, oyster sauce 6 g, garlic powder 0.8 g, chili 5 g, basil 1 g. Density/leaf-weight assumptions; iodine 0.8 mcg proxy dominated by fish sauce.

soy.basis: Per 100 g, treating 1 g as 1 mL to match the existing plan. Canadian Silk Unsweetened label per 250 mL. Iodine uses unfortified soy beverage 3.2 mcg/243 g; do not use US Silk iodine fortification.

cereal.basis: Canadian Fibre One Original 587 g label per 62 g: Ca250 mg, Fe8 mg, K150 mg, D/B12 zero. Iodine not declared; negligible trace estimate, no iodine fortification assumed.

fruit.basis: Per 100 g fruit tray: equal edible weights cantaloupe, honeydew, watermelon, pineapple, strawberry (CNF 1721/1605/1691/1734/1749). Actual fruit proportions unknown. Iodine 0.3 mcg/100 g trace proxy.
